item.title: Court orders sister to vacate farm with week’s notice as family feud continues
item.description: A February 5th B.C. Supreme Court ruling ordered Janet Baldwin to vacate the Cameo Farms property in Fort St. John, now owned by her sister, on or before February 12th.

item.title: Crown lawyer asks court to correct hunter’s record after sentencing mistake
item.description: Hunter Richard Dawson Smith pleaded guilty to violating the Wildlife Act, but when Provincial Court Judge Oliver Fleck pronounced the sentence, he inadvertently altered the wording of a order agreed under a plea bargain. Smith was later acquitted of violating that order.

item.title: Dawson Creek MMA gym’s seminars raise more than $2,500 for victims in Tumbler Ridge
item.description: MMA coach Evan Ollenberger of Dawson Creek's Legend Martial Arts Academy put on seminars featuring two veterans of the sport as a charity event to benefit the victims of the Tumbler Ridge school shooting.

item.title: Ministry cites ‘significant, unsustainable cost’ of $1.8m a bed to justify long-term care homes delay
item.description: B.C.'s Ministry of Finance says high costs have caused delays in the construction of long-term care homes in B.C., including in Fort St. John.

item.title: Fort St. John theatre group to host auditions for double-feature show
item.description: Stage North Theatre Society is holding drop-in auditions for productions of War of the Worlds and Sleepwalker on February 21st, 22nd and 28th, from 12 p.m. to 4 p.m.

item.title: Jobs Minister Ravi Kahlon says federal strategy gets “two thumbs up” from B.C.
item.description: VICTORIA — British Columbia Jobs Minister Ravi Kahlon says he will be meeting with federal Defence Minister David McGuinty to discuss shipbuilding in B.C. among other possibilities following the release of Canada’s defence industrial strategy. item.title: Police in Surrey, B.C., denied request to delay next step in transition plan: chief
item.description: SURREY — The chief of the Surrey Police Service says his force, which has been swamped with extortion cases, has been denied by the B.C. government its request to delay the transition from the RCMP. item.title: Prophet River First Nation chief named vice-chair of alliance supporting sustainable energy projects
item.description: Prophet River First Nation Chief Valerie Askoty was named vice-chair of the First Nations Natural Gas Alliance during the week of the BC Natural Resources Forum 2026 in Prince George.

item.title: ‘The true north spirit’: Performers, carving and ice burning returns to Fort St. John for Winter Fest 2026
item.description: Performers and artists entertained crowds at the Winter Fest finale in Fort St. John this weekend, which included the customary ice burning spectacle.
